test_cases.action: from the screen carrying one rendering, look for the job on the screen carrying the other and judge whether it is recognizable before tapping
test_cases.expected_result: the second rendering is recognizable as the same job
test_cases.confirms_if: a user who learned one rendering would not recognize the other on its surface
test_cases.overturns_if: surface, scope or explicit wording makes the second rendering recognizable
test_cases.observed_result: from a candidate: both renderings tapped live and open the identical Super offer. They sit on different surfaces (a promotional banner on the Shop page vs a product row on the Energy page) and both are explicit words that share "FREE" and "TRY/TRIAL", so a user who learned one would recognize the other. Justification: different surfaces, and both renderings are explicit rather than glyph-only. Noted, not weighed here: the Shop banner's family-plan face ("Save with a family plan!") leads to the individual Super offer, a banner-copy question rather than a rendering one
